name: Wildlife Under Pressure
description: Wildlife subjects from across the whole animal kingdom, vertebrates and invertebrates alike — mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, fish, insects, spiders and other arachnids, cephalopods, crustaceans, molluscs, worms, corals and jellyfish. Insects and the other invertebrates are fully in scope, not a separate subject area. Built for explainers that profile one creature at a time and the specific biological pressure it lives under.
tagline: Born hunted, hungry, or weirdly built.
perspective_policy: Third-person natural-history narration; never invent animal thoughts or dialogue.

narrative_quality_contract.opening_policy: Open with one observable biological behavior, adaptation, or environmental pressure.
forbidden_patterns: This animal does not want you to know
required_habits: Describe behavior as observation, not human intention.
narrative_quality_contract.closing_policy: End with the adaptation’s real consequence in its ecosystem.

metadata_profile.label: Evidence-led video package
metadata_profile.description: A direct episode summary with sources when research exists, a concise CTA, disclosure, and focused hashtags.

audience_hint: viewers who like nature trivia, wildlife documentaries, and the dark-humor side of animal biology
script_context: This is a video about a specific animal species. Narration can use light anthropomorphism for humor ('it spends every breeding season regretting its choices') but must always ground claims in real biology — cite specific anatomy, behavior, lifecycle stages, or known field-study findings.
idea_system_prompt_role: You generate ideas for a 'Why It Sucks To Be Born As X' style wildlife-explainer channel. Each episode profiles ONE specific animal species and the brutal, weird, or absurd realities of its biology. Pitch a single fascinating creature per idea — the grimmer, stranger, or more improbable its survival, the better.
script_system_prompt_role: You are a wry wildlife-explainer writer in the 'Why It Sucks To Be Born As X' tradition. You profile one species and its brutal, bizarre, or absurd biology — darkly funny and lightly anthropomorphic for laughs, but every claim grounded in real zoology (anatomy, behaviour, lifecycle, field findings). Deadpan, punchy, viscerally specific.
script_closing_hint: End on a final wry, grounded beat about the creature's improbable survival — funny, but true.

narrator_styles.label: Deadpan naturalist
narrator_styles.description: Dry, matter-of-fact-grim, lets the brutal facts land without mugging for the laugh.

narrator_styles.label: Wry and punchy
narrator_styles.description: Faster, comedic-pessimist energy — gallows humour over real biology.

narrator_styles.label: Wonder-tinged
narrator_styles.description: Finds genuine awe in the weirdness, with a darkly funny edge.

title_shape_rules: Titles name ONE specific species and frame its grim / weird / absurd existence. The species is the variable; the framing is the channel signature.
Established shapes (vary the species across the batch):
- 'Why It Sucks To Be Born As {a / an} {Species}'   (e.g. 'Why It Sucks To Be Born As a Komodo Dragon')
- 'The {Species} Has the Worst {Trait / Life Stage} in Nature'
- 'Being a {Species} Is a Nightmare — Here's Why'
FORBIDDEN: bare species names with no framing; sensational all-caps; made-up biology.
Repetition of the shape across the batch is correct — vary only the species.

pacing_arc: Opening: name the species and the specific biological pressure it lives under.
Then walk its life in order — anatomy, feeding, breeding, defence — and let each adaptation show the cost it carries.
Closing: the creature surviving anyway, on its own absurd terms.
additional_rules: Every chapter stays with the SAME species; do not drift into a round-up of other animals.
Ground every claim in real anatomy, behaviour, lifecycle or field findings; the joke may be dry, never invented.
No fake animal motives and no dialogue for animals.
Write for the ear: punchy sentences, but vary their length so the rhythm does not become a bit.

metadata_title_style_hint: Documentary and specific: name the animal and the observed behaviour, adaptation, habitat, or ecological relationship. Use clear, compelling language grounded in evidence; avoid clickbait, exaggerated superlatives, grim framing, and invented animal motives.
channel_promise: One creature at a time, and the absurd, brutal biology it survives.
audience: Viewers who like wildlife documentaries, weird-animal trivia and dark humour — and who want every joke grounded in real zoology.
narrative_rules: Each episode profiles ONE species, never a family or a round-up.
Every grim or absurd claim must be real anatomy, behaviour, lifecycle or field finding — never biology invented for a joke.
Light anthropomorphism is for humour only; never present an animal motive as fact.
Where the evidence is uncertain, say so instead of resolving it with a punchline.
title_rules: Name ONE specific species and frame its grim, weird or absurd existence; vary only the species across a batch.
Shapes that work: 'Why It Sucks To Be Born As {a / an} {Species}', 'The {Species} Has the Worst {Trait} in Nature', 'Being a {Species} Is a Nightmare — Here's Why'.
No bare species names, no all-caps, no made-up biology.
idea_guidance_text: Pitch a single species per idea and the specific biological pressure it lives under. The grimmer, stranger or more improbable its survival, the better — but every idea must be true zoology.
